text:
maria: Heads-up — I started a quick spike for automatic model-variant fallback when the primary model is saturated. Want to decide the routing policy + console controls before I wire the PR. :thinking:

jon: Is the trigger pure GPU capacity (OOM/slot exhaustion) or include latency/QoS signals (p99 tail latency, queue depth)?

maria: Primarily capacity (saturated workers / request rejects) + tail latency as secondary. We should avoid oscillation. Thinking 'gradual demotion' not hard cutover.

sahil: Proposed heuristic: 1) detect saturation via sliding window: rejected_req_rate > 5% OR queue_depth_avg > 0.8*slot_capacity OR p99_latency > SLO*1.5. 2) route new requests to the highest-compatible variant in same region with capacity. 3) keep sticky session for N minutes for active kv-cached sessions. 4) backoff sample to primary to detect recovery.

anya: Console/UX question — we need per-tenant and global toggles. Default: enabled for enterprise tier, opt-in for self-serve. Also support "dry-run" telemetry mode so we can observe before enforcing.

kevin: Quotas: fallback must honor tenant quotas and dedicated capacity reservations. We can mark fallback requests in billing/telemetry as "fallback_variant" so cost attribution is correct. Also do not borrow Dedicated slots from other tenants.

maria: Agree. Also need clear telemetry: count(fallbacks), latency_by_variant, success_rate_by_variant, and a small graph that shows percent traffic diverted.

jon: API surface idea: allow routes to define a fallback_policy header or route config. Example (pseudo):

```
fallback_policy: auto
fallback_order: ["compatible_same_region","quantized_variant","cheaper_variant"]
max_sticky_minutes: 5
recovery_probe_rate: 0.01
```

maria: Nice. Keep it simple in proto: mode + preference list + caps. Implementation can expand.

sahil: Implementation details: routing should prefer compatibility by schema first (same tokenizer, same output format). If exact compatibility not available, map outputs via lightweight adapter (e.g., truncate or normalize logits). Avoid cases where function-calling contracts break.

anya: UX for rollouts: enable canary where 0.5-2% traffic is diverted to candidate fallback variant first. Allow manual override and per-route "prefer_primary" switch. Also surface incident links if fallback rate spikes.

kevin: Telemetry hooks: increment metric labels {route, tenant, primary_model, fallback_model, reason=capacity}. Emit event to eventbus: model_fallback.started / .ended with small payload. That lets SRE and billing pick up.

ops-bot: Created INF-452 <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-452|INF-452> — panel for fallback telemetry (rolling window + tenant filter) :white_check_mark:

jon: Edge cases: what if fallback variant returns different tokenization lengths -> cost and latency mismatch. We should estimate token_delta and include a conservative token budget when routing. Also protect against fallback storm: add per-variant rate limiter and circuit breaker.

maria: For safety, fallback should only route new requests (not resume streaming sessions in-flight) unless adapter proves compatibility. Add a short TTL for sticky demotion so we re-evaluate.

sahil: Tests: unit tests for policy decision, integration tests simulating worker saturation, chaos tests that flip capacity. Add synthetic load tests that assert no more than X% of requests get rejected during failover.

anya: On the console, add a single toggle on route config: [ ] Auto fallback (enterprise defaults ON) and a "Dry run" checkbox. Also an audit log entry when automatic fallback occurs.

maria: Action items: 1) I'll open PR with routing-policy + circuit-breaker + marking telemetry. 2) @sahil will prototype decision function and tests. 3) @anya will mock up a small console control and a dry-run metric. 4) @kevin will wire billing tag for fallback_model. 5) Ops-bot ticket INF-452 exists for dashboards.

jon: Minor: add an opt-out header for customers that absolutely need primary (e.g., X-Prefer-Primary: true) so we don't silently divert for compliance-sensitive flows.

maria: Good call. We'll expose X-Fallback-Mode and X-Prefer-Primary headers for self-hosted/private deploys too. Example header snippet in prod: 

```
# client example
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "X-Fallback-Mode: auto" \n  -H "X-Prefer-Primary: false" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-4k","input":"..."}'
```

maria: Ok I'll draft the PR description and include telemetry/console mocks. Plan: roll canary next week behind a feature flag and enable dry-run for 48h. :rocket:

kevin: Sounds good. I'll coordinate with billing infra for tags.

ops-bot: INF-452 updated with subtask INF-453 (console toggle) and INF-454 (token_delta estimator).

maria: Thanks all — will ping when PR is ready for review.
